title: Bacterial Transformation Protocol
author: Laura Sánchez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6taheie

steps.title: Thaw competent cells
steps.instruction: Remove competent cells from -80 °C storage and thaw on ice for 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Chill DNA on ice
steps.instruction: Place approximately 5 ng (2 µL) of DNA in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube on ice. If the DNA originates from a MoClo protocol sample, add the whole 20 µL of DNA instead of 2 µL.

steps.title: Mix DNA with competent cells
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the thawed competent cells to the chilled DNA. Mix gently by pipetting up‑and‑down or flicking the tube 4–5 times; do not vortex.

steps.title: Incubate mixture on ice
steps.instruction: Leave the DNA‑cell mixture on ice for 30 minutes without further mixing.

steps.title: Heat‑shock cells
steps.instruction: Heat‑shock the tube at 42 °C for exactly 45 seconds; do not mix during the shock.

steps.title: Add recovery medium
steps.instruction: Add 950 µL of room‑temperature LB or SOC medium to the tube.

steps.title: Recover at 37 °C with shaking
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 37 °C for 60 minutes with vigorous shaking at 250 rpm or by rotating. Follow the competent‑cell manufacturer’s recommendations for recovery media and times if they differ.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic plates
steps.instruction: Prepare LB agar plates containing the appropriate antibiotic: 100 µg/mL ampicillin, 100 µg/mL kanamycin, or 50 µg/mL spectinomycin.

steps.title: Plate transformed cells and controls
steps.instruction: Spread 50–100 µL of the recovered cell suspension (or ligation mixture) onto each antibiotic plate, include controls, and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Spread 50–100 µL of cells onto each plate
Include a negative‑control plate (agar without cells)
Include a positive‑control plate (cells transformed with pUC)
Optional tip: pellet remaining cells, resuspend in 50–100 µL and plate to capture all transformants

steps.title: Check plate contamination
steps.instruction: Inspect the plates for contaminant colonies; if none are observed, continue the protocol.

steps.title: Pick three positive colonies
steps.instruction: From each plate, select three well‑isolated positive colonies, streak each onto a fresh LB‑antibiotic plate keeping the strains separated, and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Inoculate liquid cultures
steps.instruction: Prepare liquid inocula for each of the three selected colonies in 15 mL Falcon tubes.

substeps.instruction: Pick a colony with an inoculating loop
Resuspend it in 5 mL LB containing the same antibiotic as the plate
Incubate at 37 °C overnight with shaking (colonies large enough may allow steps 11 and 12 to be combined)

steps.title: Harvest cells for miniprep
steps.instruction: Transfer 1.5 mL of each overnight culture into a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge (Eppendorf) tube and perform a plasmid miniprep.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 1.5 mL culture into an Eppendorf tube

steps.title: Verify plasmids
steps.instruction: Analyze the purified plasmids using the Plasmid Verification Protocol and/or DNA sequencing.
